National Weather Service New York NY
422 AM EDT Sat Mar 14 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Highlighted potential for strong winds for portions of the
region in the Hazardous Weather Outlook for Monday night. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Steepening pressure gradient will bring a very gusty westerly
flow today with gusts approaching near 40 mph.

2) Strong frontal system Monday into Monday night with periods 
of heavy rain, potentially strong winds and a chance of 
thunderstorms. There is also the possibility of coastal flooding
near times of high tide.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
.KEY MESSAGE 1... 
Steepening pressure gradient will bring a very gusty westerly
flow today with gusts approaching near 40 mph. This comes from a
passing low pressure wave to the north and high pressure that
will start to build in from the west. Model BUFKIT soundings
indicate top of mixed layer to reach mostly 40 to 45 mph,
keeping wind gusts below advisory levels. However, a localized
peak gust to 45 to 50 mph will be possible.

This will make for a cooler than normal day and for temperatures
to feel quite cooler than their actual values. While most high
temperature values are in the 40s, the apparent temperatures
will be more in the mid 30s to near 40.

.KEY MESSAGE 2... 
Strong frontal system Monday into Monday night with periods of 
heavy rain, potentially strong winds and a chance of 
thunderstorms. There is also the possibility of coastal flooding
near times of high tide.

Increasing dynamics and a strong low level jet will be the main
factors driving a system and cold front for Monday into Monday
night. NBM showing increased probabilities for wind gusts to
exceed 55 mph. NAM low level jet near 2-3kft of nearly 90 kt 
with GFS indicating the low level jet near 2-3kft close to 70-75
kt.

This forcing will also mean a high shear environment. Even with
limited elevated instability, there will be sufficient factors
to give a chance of thunderstorms. With any thunderstorms, there
is also the conditional probability of the thunderstorm
potentially giving damaging winds. SPC has western parts of the
region in a marginal risk for severe weather. The primary threat
with the thunderstorms would be damaging winds.

Heavy rain probable with the system as well with this vertical
forcing. The deep trough will help increase precipitable waters
to near 1.5 inches, above the max climatology for March 16th
according to OKX sounding climatology. Considering the parallel
flow low to upper levels, training of cells looks likely so
multiple rounds of heavy rain may be in store. There is marginal
risk for flooding as a result. Mainly poor drainage, urban and
low lying nuisance flooding expected but localized flash
flooding cannot be ruled out.

Coastal flooding and beach erosion are possible with this system 
given the expected magnitude of S flow and associated wave action, 
also with astronomical tides increasing with the approach of a new 
moon next Wednesday. However, tide levels are quite low leading
up to the event, which may help limit the magnitude of any
coastal flooding. Surge guidance looks a bit low with surge of 
only about 1 to 1.5 ft. Adding a half foot to this guidance signals
potential for minor coastal flooding with the high tides Mon 
and Mon night. This may be most problematic for the south shore
back Bays of Nassau, western Great South Bay, and western Long 
Island Sound.

&&

.AVIATION /09Z SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
A cold front moves through the area early this morning. Weak 
high pressure builds this afternoon into the, moving over the 
area tonight.

VFR.

Winds W/SW less than 10 kt with speeds increasing to 15-25 kt
during the day, peaking late morning into the afternoon. Gusts 
begin to develop around daybreak increasing to 30-35 kt. A few 
gusts up to 40-43 kt possible. Winds and gusts begin to diminish
late afternoon, with gusts quickly ending after sunset.


 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty... 

A few gusts up to 40 kt possible Saturday afternoon.


.OUTLOOK FOR 06Z SUNDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY... 

Late tonight: VFR.

Sunday: VFR. SE wind gusts 15-20 kt. 

Sunday night: MVFR or lower with rain becoming likely. SE wind gusts 
near 20 kt, increasing to near 30 kt by daybreak Monday.

Monday: MVFR or lower with rain. A chance of thunderstorms.
Winds become more southerly with gusts near 30-40 kt. Potential peak 
gusts Monday night to 45 kt. Winds decrease slightly and become more 
westerly late Monday night, gusts 25-35 kt.

Tuesday: Rain tapers off, possible mix with snow before all 
precipitation ends in AM. MVFR or lower possible early, otherwise 
improving conditions to VFR by afternoon. WSW gusts 25- 30 kt.

Wednesday: VFR with light W/SW winds.

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component forecasts, 
can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

&&

.MARINE...
A lull in the winds currently with ocean seas near 5 ft.
Expecting the westerly winds to increase today as the low 
pressure wave passes to the north with deep mixing expected.
This will allow for gusty winds today, highest late this morning
into the afternoon. Wind gusts on all waters are expected to get
back into SCA range this morning and then gales in the latter
half of this morning into the afternoon. For tonight, the winds
trend down to SCA range for this evening and then overnight are
forecast to fall below SCA thresholds. Ocean seas stay in SCA 
range this evening and then eventually fall below SCA levels 
overnight.

After a brief lull in conditions Sunday with widespread below
SCA conditions, conditions ramp up Sunday night and further more
on Monday into Monday night. Expecting widespread SCA level wind
gusts to develop Sunday night followed by potential for gale to
storm force winds Monday into Monday night. Ocean seas likely
remain at SCA levels through midweek while winds do trend
downward going into midweek. SCA potential winds for Tuesday and
eventually below SCA levels for Wednesday.
